title: Indian Princesses by Eliana Theologides Rodriguez at Atlantic Theater...
transcript: This play about transracial parenting is hysterical and devastating. It features a bunch of people who've been fantastic in everything I've seen them in, such as Haley Wong, Lark White and Greg Keller, and it features some subject matter that I'm actually quite familiar with. Basically, it's about these five young girls of color and their white fathers coming together in a program meant to foster bonding and education. Aside from being woefully culturally offensive in various ways, the program also raises questions and conversations that some of the dads are completely unprepared to have. Watching them try to navigate these moments is equally funny and infuriating, but the emotional core of the story comes from the daughters. All of the actresses, who are adults, are given a difficult assignment here — portraying the experience of having big realizations without the vocabulary to express them, due to age and context. While the play doesn't feel fully structurally sound and doesn't yet stick the landing, it's in great shape for having just started previews. I also see a lot of inherent value in how this piece addresses an interesting and underrepresented subject, and better yet, does so in both a nuanced and sufficiently entertaining way. With that, another program for my collection.
